blueprint.name: Mirror the BNK supply chain into JFrog Artifactory
blueprint.description: Replicate the F5 Artifact Repository into a JFrog Artifactory you already run, then verify every artifact against the BOM. Nothing is created in IBM Cloud and no cluster is needed — replication copies registry-to-registry, so the mirror can be seeded as a supply-chain step long before an air-gapped cluster exists. Follows Appendix B of the roksbnkctl book; requires roksbnkctl v1.49.0+.

outcomes: Every BNK image and OCI-packaged Helm chart replicated into your Artifactory repository
`registry verify` confirming all artifacts present and digest-matched
A mirror a disconnected ROKS cluster can install from

prerequisites.description: An IBM Cloud credential template on the project. It is used only to reach the supply-chain COS bucket holding the FAR auth tarball and subscription JWT — no IBM Cloud infrastructure is created or touched.

A LOCAL Docker repository in Artifactory, created beforehand through its UI or REST API. It must be local: a remote repository is a read-through cache and cannot be pushed to. Artifactory OSS has no Docker repository type at all — Pro, Enterprise or Cloud is required.
An access token with Deploy/Cache and Read on that repository. A dedicated account with a token is the right shape: it is scoped, and it can be revoked without disturbing a human login.
The supply-chain COS bucket holding the FAR auth tarball and the subscription JWT. These are the entitlement material FAR itself requires and are not served from the mirror.

input_summary.label: Repository path, not subdomain
input_summary.value: roksbnkctl composes references as <host>/<repo prefix>/<image>, which is Artifactory's repository-path form. If your instance uses the subdomain method instead (bnk-mirror.artifactory.example.com/f5-tmm), put the full subdomain host in the host field and leave the repository prefix EMPTY. Getting this wrong surfaces as 404 / repository not found, which reads like the prefix is wrong rather than like the access method differs.

input_summary.label: Username and token are both required
input_summary.value: JFrog needs the account the token was issued to as the username, and the token as the password. Sending the token as the username instead returns 401 — verified against a live JFrog Container Registry 7.161.16. The username is the token's `sub` claim: decode the JWT and take the name after /users/.

input_summary.label: Private CA
input_summary.value: Supply the CA only if Artifactory presents a certificate from a private CA. Record it from the file that issued the certificate, not by capturing it from the connection — a CA learned over the connection it is meant to authenticate proves nothing. When it is set, replicate never dials the registry to discover trust.

input_summary.label: verify is the step that means anything
input_summary.value: replicate reports what it pushed; verify independently re-reads the BOM and checks each artifact against the digest it should have, so a partial copy or a tag that moved underneath you is caught. Treat replicate succeeding as progress and verify succeeding as done.

input_summary.label: Teardown
input_summary.value: Destroy is a no-op unless 'Delete artifacts on destroy' is set. Emptying a registry you already run is rarely what you want, and never what you want when the registry outlives this deployment.

required.name: artifactory_host
required.label: Artifactory host
required.description: Hostname serving the Docker repository, without a scheme. For a repository-path instance this is the Artifactory host itself; for a subdomain instance it is the full per-repository subdomain.

required.name: artifactory_repo_prefix
required.label: Repository prefix (the local Docker repository key)
required.description: The repository key artifacts nest under, forming <host>/<prefix>/<image>. Leave EMPTY on a subdomain instance, where the repository is already encoded in the host.

required.name: artifactory_username
required.label: Artifactory username
required.description: The account the token was issued to. For a JFrog access token this is the token's `sub` claim — decode the JWT and take the name after /users/, e.g. "jfac@…/users/admin" means admin. It is NOT optional and the token cannot stand in for it: JFrog rejects the token-as-username form with 401, verified against a live 7.161.16 instance. Anonymous push works only if your instance permits it, in which case both fields can be left blank.

required.name: artifactory_token
required.label: Artifactory access token
required.description: An access token with Deploy/Cache and Read on the repository, sent as the password alongside the username above. Stored base64 in the workspace config — obfuscation, not encryption — and passed to the step as an environment variable, never on the command line.

required.name: region
required.label: IBM Cloud region
required.description: Region of the supply-chain COS bucket's credentials. Inherits from the selected credential template. No IBM Cloud infrastructure is created.

required.name: resource_group
required.label: Resource group
required.description: IBM Cloud resource group. Inherits from the selected credential template.

required.name: cos_bucket
required.label: Supply-chain COS bucket
required.description: Bucket holding the FAR auth tarball and subscription JWT. Account-suffixed buckets (bnk-artifacts-<account>) must be named explicitly.

optional.name: artifactory_ca_b64
optional.label: Artifactory root CA (base64 PEM)
optional.description: Base64 PEM of the CA that issued Artifactory's certificate. Needed ONLY when that certificate comes from a private CA — leave blank for a publicly trusted certificate. Already base64: it is stored verbatim. Setting it stops replicate from dialling the registry to discover trust. If a run fails with 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority', this is what is missing — and on a load-balanced instance the CA that issued the certificate actually in use may not be the one issued to the origin.

optional.name: artifactory_ca_sha256
optional.label: Certificate SHA-256 pin
optional.description: Optional pin of the served chain, enforced during the TLS handshake. Accepts bare hex, sha256:…, colon-separated, or raw `openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256` output.

optional.name: prefix
optional.label: Workspace prefix
optional.description: Names the roksbnkctl workspace this replication runs in. It creates no IBM Cloud resources, so this is bookkeeping rather than a naming scheme.

optional.name: manifest_version
optional.label: BNK manifest version
optional.description: The BNK release whose BOM is replicated. Blank = the roksbnkctl default.

optional.name: cos_instance
optional.label: Supply-chain COS instance
optional.description: COS instance holding the FAR auth key + subscription JWT. Blank = bnk-supply-chain.

optional.name: cos_region
optional.label: Supply-chain COS region
optional.description: Region of that bucket. Blank = us-south.

optional.name: far_auth_file
optional.label: FAR auth object name
optional.description: Object name of the FAR auth tarball in the bucket. Blank = f5-far-auth-key.tgz.

optional.name: subscription_jwt_file
optional.label: Subscription JWT object name
optional.description: Object name of the subscription JWT in the bucket. Blank = subscription.jwt.

optional.name: delete_artifacts_on_destroy
optional.label: Delete artifacts on destroy
optional.description: Set true to remove every replicated artifact from Artifactory when this deployment is destroyed. Blank (the default) leaves the mirror in place — the usual answer for a registry you already run and that outlives this deployment.

optional.name: ibmcloud_api_key
optional.label: IBM Cloud API key
optional.description: Filled from the project's credential template at creation. Used only to read the supply-chain objects from COS.

optional.name: icr_host
optional.label: Icr host
optional.description: ICRHost overrides the IBM Container Registry host for target=icr (e.g. Maps to config.yaml registry.icr_host.

optional.name: icr_namespace
optional.label: Icr namespace
optional.description: The ICR namespace artifacts nest under for target=icr. Maps to config.yaml registry.icr_namespace.

optional.name: registry_include_deps
optional.label: Registry include deps
optional.description: IncludeDeps unions the non-F5 dependency artifacts (Jetstack cert-manager chart + images, the bitnami/kubectl node-labeler image) into the BOM. Maps to config.yaml registry.include_deps.

optional.name: registry_namespace
optional.label: Registry namespace
optional.description: The mirror project the artifacts land in. Maps to config.yaml registry.namespace.

optional.name: source_service_account_b64
optional.label: Source service account b64
optional.description: The FAR `_json_key_base64` service-account JSON, base64-encoded, used as the replication SOURCE credential for repo.f5.com. Maps to config.yaml registry.source_service_account_b64.

modules.name: roksbnkctl FAR Mirror
modules.description: init -> registry replicate --target generic -> registry verify, against your Artifactory. Creates no infrastructure.
